# Cowait

> Cowait for Claude Code is a free, open-source (MIT) terminal side panel that sits next to Claude Code. Through Claude Code hooks it groups the files each Claude turn changed, shows their diffs, counts a file as reviewed only after it has been on screen long enough, and relays one-line notes from the user to Claude on its next tool call without interrupting the turn. Between turns it offers a daily stack-machine puzzle, a turn-based card roguelike (Debug Dungeon), a typing game that uses the code Claude just wrote, and spaced-repetition flashcards.

Key facts:

- Install: `npm install -g cowait-cli` (the command is `cowait`); Node.js 20 or newer. Or from source: `git clone https://github.com/JaspinXu/Cowait.git`, then `npm install -g .` inside it.
- First run: `cowait split` opens the panel in a pane next to Claude Code (Windows Terminal, tmux, zellij, WezTerm, kitty, iTerm2); a welcome screen hooks up the current project with one key (`cowait install --project` does the same).
- Works on Windows, macOS and Linux. Interface in English and Chinese.
- Runs locally: no account, no telemetry. Network use is optional: a daily npm version check, and the topic or recent diffs when the user asks an AI model (Haiku) to write flashcards.
- Design choices: rewards come from reviewing and from Claude's results (a working turn, passing tests), never from time spent waiting; quick approvals of unread changes do not count toward review coverage.
- Author: Zhaobin Xu (GitHub: JaspinXu). Repository: https://github.com/JaspinXu/Cowait
